lines.say: One ring, six seconds. Your receptionist can't answer.
lines.direction: Reel 6 HOOK, narrator, from f10 after the frame-0 trill rings out, over a giant clock that has just stepped one second: calm, close and dry, an owner naming a fact and then the moment, not an ad. "One ring, six seconds" even and unhurried (a fact the viewer can feel; heard by about 1.3 s); a natural sentence pause; "Your receptionist can't answer" warm, with empathy, never blame (she is busy with someone, never replaced: ig1's stance). "receptionist" said plainly (it is the TikTok search word). Target 3.4 s or less; the whole hook plus ig6-02a must end by f174 (SCRIPT.md §1.3). Screens S1a [0-3] "One ring," / "six seconds." (set at frame 0) and S1b [4-7] "Your receptionist" / "can't answer."
lines.speak: One ring, six seconds. Your receptionist can't answer.

lines.direction: Reel 6 beat 2, FIRST HALF of a sentence that ring 2 interrupts (SCRIPT.md §4 b2): it must sound UNFINISHED, a light continuing lift on "rings,", not a full stop. Synthesise several candidates and pick by ear for the continuation. Placed at about f120, it must END BY f174 (ring 2 lands at f180 on the dot). Screen S2a [0-2] "While it" / "rings,".

Reel 6 beat 2, SECOND HALF, placed at ring 2 + 10 f (f190): it completes ig6-02a's sentence after the ring, so it starts mid-thought (no new-sentence attack), with a quiet weight on "still" and a settled fall on "waiting." Display: the big lockup shows "Someone's" capitalised; the tier keeps "someone's". Screen S2b [0-2] "Someone's" / "still waiting."

lines.say: A missed call is someone else's customer.
lines.direction: Reel 6 beat 3, over the whole ring clock filling with black stretches: the house opinion (voice.md position 1), said plainly and a little lower, never alarmist, no emphasis on "missed". "someone else's customer" lands as a quiet truth. Screen S3 [4-6] "Someone else's" / "customer." with the full line in the tier.
lines.speak: A missed call is someone else's customer.

lines.say: Our AI receptionist picks up, day or night.
lines.direction: Reel 6 PAYOFF, narrator, spoken out of the stop-time silence right after the hub stamps teal (the pickup): warm and settled, a small real lift on "receptionist" (the keyword, underlined on screen), a natural comma pause, then "day or night" easy and confident. Never "first ring" (truth judge T-C1). Screens S4a [0-2] "Our AI" / "receptionist" and S4b [3-7] "Picks up," / "day or night."
lines.speak: Our AI receptionist picks up, day or night.

lines.direction: Reel 6 beat 5, over the agent's clock sweeping a whole day: easy and plain; "from your words" is the product's promise (answers only from what the owner wrote), not a boast. Screen S5 [0-4] "It answers" / "from your words."

Reel 6 beat 6, an invitation with a half-smile (the trial's free test calls), not a dare shouted. Short and warm. TRIM T1 drops this line if the measured takes would push the CTA past f765. Screen S6 [0-2] "Ring it" / "yourself."

Reel 6 CTA, narrator, a fresh ig6 take (the pipeline allows exactly one borrow, ig1-07): confident, slightly lower and warm. speak has "agent" in lowercase so Sonic does not spell it out. Must END BY f765 (impact f780 − 15). Screen S7 [0-4] "Comment" / "AGENT".
